quotes.text: People ask how I stay calm during hearings and the honest answer is that I was a prosecutor for a long time, and a prosecutor learns very early that the person across the table who is sweating is probably not going to be you.

quotes.text: The thing about a filibuster that nobody tells you when you get there is that you start out thinking it's a principled act of protest and by hour four you are mostly just trying to remember if you had lunch.
quotes.speaker: Rand Paul
quotes.context: Remarks at the Young Americans for Liberty National Convention, Washington D.C., July 2018
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Rand has conducted real filibusters and spoken about them with a kind of wry, almost libertarian self-deprecation. The tell is 'mostly just trying to remember if you had lunch,' which is a perfectly constructed comic landing that real exhausted senators probably don't articulate so neatly.

quotes.text: Nothing so dates a man as to decry the younger generation.
quotes.speaker: Adlai Stevenson II
quotes.context: The Democratic statesman, in a speech at the University of Wisconsin, Madison (8 October 1952) - a dry, self-aware needle at those who complain about the young.

quotes.text: I will say, nobody warned me that about forty percent of this job is just standing very still while someone explains a chart to you. And you have to look like the chart is genuinely moving you.

quotes.text: I am the man who accompanied Jacqueline Kennedy to Paris, and I have enjoyed it.
quotes.speaker: John F. Kennedy
quotes.context: Self-deprecating opening line at a press luncheon at the Palais de Chaillot in Paris on June 2, 1961, during a state visit to France.
